The Old Dragon's Head, known natively as Laolongtou (老龙头), marks the breathtaking easternmost terminus of the Ming Dynasty Great Wall where it dramatically stone-marches 23 metres directly out into the Bhai Sea. The nickname comes from the striking visual image of the seaside watchtower resembling a massive dragon lowering its head to take a drink from the ocean.
